title: Bayesian optimization guides complex nanoparticle heterostructures
summary: Learning from earlier synthesis and microscopy data guided a human-supervised nanoparticle campaign. Researchers reported the desired structures for 18 of 19 selected candidates, including complex multielement particles. This success rate concerns a curated experimental set, not the full predicted composition space. Structural synthesis was demonstrated; catalytic and device performance were not.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization of composition and morphology

evidence.tested: Synthesized candidates were examined by microscopy and elemental analysis.
evidence.unknown: Functional performance, general search-space success and independent replication were not established.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization of composition and morphology supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary article metadata, affiliations, selected experimental Results and discussion; supplements not reviewed.
